newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS to change Elektrowatt split procedure.
newsitem.headline: CS to change Elektrowatt split procedure.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group said it was changing the procedure in its planned split-up of Elektrowatt AG so that the company will not be split up into Watt Ltd and a new Electrowatt Ltd until it has been transferred to the new owners.

Credit Suisse said it was making this technical change in the procedure as the result of a difference in opinion between the Zurich cantonal and the Swiss federal tax authorities regarding the spin-off of Watt Ltd.
Under the modified plan, Credit Suisse said it will now make the public shareholders of the present Elektrowatt a takeover offer at a price of 550 Swiss francs per share, subject to due diligence.
The 550 per share price corresponds to the total proposed purchase prices to be paid by Siemens AG and by the Swiss/German consortium.

Credit Suisse Group has a 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt, which currently comprises various energy and industrial activities. It has been seeking to divest itself of its Elektrowatt holdings for some time.
The first step of its planned divestment plan is to split Elektrowatt into two units with its energy activities grouped in a company to be called Watt AG.

Following this Credit Suisse agreed to sell its stake in Watt to a Swiss-German consortium and last month Credit Suisse said electronics group Siemens would take over its stake in Elektrowatt's industrial activities. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
